final.reason: Budget exhausted (6/6 physical evaluations) without a passing design, so FEASIBLE is not established; and since a curated search failure is not a full-domain proof, INFEASIBLE is not justified either. Measurements give a consistent diagnosis: (1) delivered=0/faults=4/false=0 was invariant across C=95-320 uF, gate=2.2-2.9 V, threshold=0.15-0.55 V, so the blocker is mechanical tuning, not storage/boot/wake setpoints; (2) stress/travel slack (<1, safe) depends only on main length (aux 21 vs 23 mm gave identical slack), so the aux beam is safety-neutral and can be tuned to 210 Hz freely; (3) main-length deflection shows resonance peaks near ~24 and ~34 mm with a trough at ~30-32 mm, indicating the legacy 30 mm main beam is off-resonance from the 45 Hz/0.15 g background, whose harvest optimum appears near ~34 mm. Best next design (untested due to budget): main ~34 mm (or ~24 mm for the higher mode), aux tuned toward 210 Hz, larger storage (~300 uF) for a full sample+infer+TX buffer above the 1.8 V brownout, gate reachable at resonance, and a low threshold. No false reports were ever produced, so nuisance rejection by digital confirmation is already working.
